_source: Gatev, Goetzmann and Rouwenhorst (2006), 'Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule', Review of Financial Studies 19(3) 797-827. Values read from `pdftotext -layout pairs-trading-performance-of-a-relative-value-arbitrage-rule_final.pdf` (repo root).

_provenance.table9_panel_b: p. 825, rows 'B. Short recalls on high volume' (four portfolio columns: Top 5, Top 20, 20 after top 100, All).
_provenance.table1_panel_b: pp. 806-807, rows 'B. Excess return distribution (one day waiting)' - the same wait-one-day rule without recalls, so the claim's arithmetic is Table 1B minus Table 9B.
_provenance.table9_note: p. 825: 'Panel B reports the summary statistics for the rule that waits one day before opening and closing the position.' 474 monthly observations, July 1963 - December 2002, Newey-West six-lag standard errors, absolute kurtosis.
_provenance.claim_prose: p. 824: 'The profits decline slightly by 4-13 bp per month, yet they remain large and positive. For example, the top 20 pairs portfolio earns an average of 85 bp per month with short recalls, with a Newey-West t-statistic of 9.07.'
